claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a concentrated, single-phase alloy.
Atomic-scale disorder and local lattice distortions are intrinsic to the HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
HfNbTaTiZr specimens containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen can be represented within the proposed framework.
An ab initio-based, machine-learning-enhanced interatomic potential can capture local lattice distortions and force-constant variations in HfNbTaTiZr.
A two-temperature treatment can independently represent phonon and electron heat transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Below 200 K, the lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr are comparable.
The high-temperature applicability regime is 300–1200 K for HfNbTaTiZr specimens with controlled oxygen levels.
Local lattice distortions and force-constant variations modulate phonon-scattering rates.
Atomic-scale lattice disorder modulates electron relaxation times.
Separately representing local lattice variations and temperature-dependent phonon and electron scattering will generate independent lattice and electronic conductivity channels.
Independent treatment of the two channels avoids conflating lattice and electronic heat transport.
Explicit treatment of atomic disorder and impurities will better represent thermal transport than earlier analytical approaches.
The framework will reduce uncertainty in predicted total thermal conductivity by approximately a factor of ten relative to earlier models.
The framework will correctly reproduce a crossover between lattice and electronic conductivity contributions across the specified temperature regimes.
A lattice/electronic crossover in HfNbTaTiZr has been observed experimentally.
Earlier methods relied on simplified Debye-temperature estimates or conflated lattice and electronic transport.
Earlier methods had broad error bounds and could not accurately resolve the individual lattice and electronic contributions.
The proposed predictions apply to nominally defect-free and approximately 1 wt.% oxygen-containing HfNbTaTiZr within the stated temperature windows.
Extrapolation outside the below-200 K and 300–1200 K regimes is uncertain.
The effects of impurity concentration and the relationship between local distortion and macroscopic transport remain quantitatively uncertain.
